summary: The small DOM toolkit and the formatters shared by almost every frontend module. Its centrepiece is the `html` tagged template, which escapes every interpolated value unless it is already `html` or `raw` output, so rendering API data through `innerHTML` is **XSS-safe by default** and unescaped markup has to be requested explicitly. It also provides the `$`/`$$` query shortcuts, `mount`, and the `fmt` helpers that turn the backend's naive-UTC timestamps and raw numbers into display strings.

notes.text: Header comment stating the module's key promise: `html` escapes every interpolated value unless it is itself `html` or `raw` output, so **XSS safety is the default** and only deliberate code can insert unescaped markup.
`$` is a short alias for `querySelector` (first match, or `null`). The optional `root` narrows the search, e.g. `$('[data-uptime]', view)` only looks inside the current page.
`$$` returns **all** matches as a real array (by spreading the `NodeList`), so callers can use `map`, `filter` and `forEach` directly.
The five characters that are special in HTML, mapped to their entity equivalents.

`esc()` makes any value safe to place in HTML: `??` turns `null` and `undefined` into an empty string, then every special character is replaced. Escaping both kinds of quote makes the result safe inside attribute values too.

`SafeHTML` is a marker wrapper meaning 'this string is markup that is already escaped or trusted'. Its `toString()` returns the markup, so `String(x)` or assigning it to `innerHTML` yields the plain string.

`raw()` is the explicit opt-out: it marks a string as safe so `html` inserts it without escaping. It is meant only for markup the code builds itself (icon SVGs, chart fragments), never for API or user data.

`render` decides how one interpolated value becomes text. `null`, `undefined` and `false` render as nothing, so a template can write `${isOpen && badge}` and get an empty string when the condition is false.
Arrays are rendered item by item and joined, so `${items.map(...)}` can produce a whole list without a manual `join`.
Values that are already `SafeHTML` (nested `html` templates or `raw`) pass through untouched, which prevents double escaping.
Everything else, including strings and numbers from the API, is escaped.

`html` is a **tagged template** function: writing `html` directly before a template literal makes JavaScript call it with `strings` (the literal chunks) and `values` (the results of the `${}` expressions), always with one more chunk than values.
Starts the output with the first literal chunk.
For each value, appends its rendered (escaped) form followed by the next literal chunk, rebuilding the template in order.
Returns the result wrapped as `SafeHTML`, so it can be nested inside another `html` template, or passed to `mount()`, without being escaped twice.
`mount(el, content)` replaces an element's content and returns the element, so calls can be chained.
Assigns `String(content)` to `innerHTML`; the content is normally an `html` result, so everything interpolated into it has already been escaped. Then returns the element.
Section marker: formatting helpers.
Two `Intl.NumberFormat` instances, created once and reused because building one per call is slower: `NUMBER` adds thousands separators (`12,345`) and `MONEY` formats US dollars (`$1,234.50`).

`utc()` parses backend timestamps. The API sends naive UTC strings with no zone (see `iip/clock.py`) and `new Date()` would read those as **local** time, so a `Z` is appended unless the string already carries a `Z` or an offset like `+02:00`; empty input gives `null`.
`fmt` groups the display formatters used throughout the UI.
`num` rounds to a whole number and adds separators; `?? 0` stops a missing value from printing 'NaN'.
`money` formats as US dollars, treating a missing value as 0.
`pct` turns a fraction into a percentage string with `digits` decimals, so 0.256 becomes `26%`.
`time` shows hours and minutes in the viewer's own locale and time zone on a 24-hour clock (`hourCycle` set to `h23`). `?.` and `??` print an em dash when there is no timestamp.
`dateTime` does the same with a short month and day added, e.g. `Oct 2, 14:03`.

`ago` produces relative times: it parses the timestamp, prints an em dash if it is missing, and measures the age in seconds. Subtracting a `Date` converts it to milliseconds, and `Math.max(0, ...)` clamps slightly-future times (small clock differences) to zero.
Buckets the age: under 45 seconds is 'just now', then minutes, hours and finally days, each rounded to the nearest whole unit.
`duration` splits a number of seconds into days, hours, minutes and seconds using integer division (`Math.floor`) and remainders (`%`).
Shows only the two most significant units, e.g. `2d 4h`, `3h 12m`, `5m 9s` or `42s`; the Integration page uses it for the server's uptime.
`initials` turns a name into up to two capital letters for avatars ('Ada Lovelace' becomes 'AL'), using '?' when the name is missing.
`type` maps event-type codes from the API to readable labels, falling back to the raw code for anything unknown. The last line closes `fmt`.
`LEVELS` lists the risk levels from lowest to highest; components use the position in this list, e.g. to decide how many severity pips to light.

`levelOf` converts a 0-100 score into a level using the same thresholds as `LEVELS` in `iip/rules.py` (80 critical, 60 high, 30 medium), so charts colour values exactly as the backend classifies them.

`debounce` returns a wrapper that restarts a timer on every call, so `fn` only runs once calls have paused for `ms` milliseconds. The Events search box uses it so typing does not fire one request per keystroke, and the Risk Lab uses it to batch quick toggles.
`sleep` returns a Promise that resolves after `ms` milliseconds, so async code can simply `await sleep(260)` between steps, as the boot sequence does.
`trapTab(container, e)` keeps keyboard focus inside a modal. The drawer and the palette are marked `aria-modal`, but Tab used to walk out of them into the page behind.
Only Tab presses matter, and only for an existing container.
Every control that can take focus, keeping only visible ones: `offsetParent` is `null` for elements hidden with `display: none`.
Nothing focusable means nothing to trap. Otherwise: the first and last controls, and whether focus is currently on one of them (it may be on the container itself).
Shift+Tab on the first control (or from outside the list) jumps to the last; Tab on the last jumps to the first. `preventDefault` stops the browser's own move.
Closes `trapTab()`.
